title.en: Exact and approximate values, and patterns in products

text.en:
The newspaper said 'about 5 lakh people came to the fair' while the gate counted 4,87,236.
"Which is right?" asked Ravi.

An exact value is the precise number, such as 4,87,236. An approximate value is a rounded number close to it, such as about 5 lakh. We use approximate values when exactness is not needed.
To round to the nearest lakh, look at the digit in the ten-thousands place. 4,87,236 has 8 there, so it rounds up to 5,00,000.
Patterns in products appear with powers of 10: multiplying by 10 adds a zero, and 1 lakh times 10 is 10 lakh.

prompt.en: A friend says an approximate value is always exact. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: It is useful when exact is not needed.

points.en: Exact is precise, approximate is rounded.
